scope.title: Candidate and source identity
scope.boundary: Real source/file/Git identity, candidate seals and current qualification admission. Small synthetic archives prove binding rules only; the separately named integration fixture uses real builders, packed CLI and local installs.

initial_state: Private ReleaseCandidateTests setup with authored 0.5.1 patch intent. candidate() writes synthetic package.tgz/adapter.zip, source=a repeated 40, prepared=b repeated 40, latest channel and three required checks (profile, preflight, release-integrity) passing.
Private package.json version 0.5.1, actual validate-release.py main loaded through runpy, and only the current profile/notes added by each case.

Clone the repository to a private Git root, copy current authored scripts/skills/templates/workflows/tests/model documents and package outputs, and commit them with synthetic 0.5.1 patch intent. Use private npm cache/log directories. Build actual archives/tarball and use local bare Git evidence plus FixtureHostedServices; all publication providers remain local substitutes.
Private Git repository with a committed README and independently captured trusted commit.

cases.title: Qualification binds the exact authored source and runtime inputs
cases.risk: Qualification runs or approves different code from the reviewed candidate basis.

conditions: Use real private Git and the candidate fixture. Capture the selected immutable source/range and runtime identity before mutation.
Independently change nested code/resources or ignored loaded runtime content, restore each change, add bytecode, or symlink an owned module directory.

when: Compute and verify source/CI subject identity; attempt preparation with loaded code differing from the selected source.
then: Authored and loaded runtime changes invalidate the original basis; restoration re-establishes it. Bytecode alone does not change authored identity.
Symlinked source and mismatched loaded/selected code reject before build; CI resolves one immutable source range.

gaps: CI subject verification includes ignored runtime and checked source: The method verifies the initial subject and restores both mutated files, but does not call ci_subject again after each restoration. Add those calls to demonstrate recovery explicitly.

cases.title: A candidate seal admits only complete, contained and unchanged artifacts
cases.risk: A formally sealed descriptor hides changed, unsafe or insufficiently checked publication inputs.

conditions: Seal and successfully verify a valid candidate first. Mutate artifact bytes, manifest destination/channel, path/type/size, required check result or evidence ref independently.

when: Seal or verify the mutated candidate using its original identity.
then: Changed bytes or material manifest facts invalidate the old identity.
Unsafe artifact names, symlinks/nonregular files, boolean sizes, unknown/nonpassing required checks and evidence/source-ref collision reject before publication.
Neither rebuilding nor a newly computed seal grants the old approval to different bytes.

gaps: Artifact and manifest edits invalidate an existing seal: The artifact test verifies its baseline; the manifest mutation test does not. Add a successful verify_candidate assertion before its mutation so unrelated invalid setup cannot satisfy rejection.

cases.title: CI preparation cannot fall back to unchecked source or authorize publication
cases.risk: A prepared-check failure becomes a signal to validate the wrong subject.

conditions: Use the real isolated CI preparation path; separately introduce a candidate verification failure and an existing release tag.

when: Prepare/check the CI subject through its actual entrypoint.
then: A failed prepared subject fails the command without source-mode fallback.
An existing public tag can permit isolated CI qualification while blocking release eligibility; CI success confers no publication permission.

cases.title: The actual packed candidate carries the qualified metadata and installs
cases.risk: Individually valid source, archives and package refer to different subjects.

conditions: Use real-build with actual archive/package builders and the packed CLI. Keep all provider operations local substitutes.

when: Build the archives, generate bundled metadata/index, pack, qualify and install both current targets from the exact candidate.
Repeat qualification with wrong release facts or secret-bearing notes while retaining a good tarball.
then: Source, archive bytes, bundled metadata/index digests, receipt and installed CLI all describe the same selected candidate; both target installs use those archives.
Good package bytes cannot conceal inconsistent release facts or secret-bearing notes.
This proves the Release composition with Packaging/Installation; public registry availability and live installation require separate observed evidence.

cases.title: Current qualification needs an explicit matching source, profile and receipt
cases.risk: Current qualification implicitly executes a retired historical recipe.

conditions: Use current-source with package 0.5.1 and its matching profile, plus a prior receipt snapshot. Select a different supported synthetic version to test admission independently of a newest-version list.

when: Qualify matching current input; independently request historical replay, omit the profile, mismatch source/tag/recorded commit or fail preparation. Inspect any resulting receipt.
then: Matching current inputs are admitted regardless of their numeric fixture version; receipts use portable artifact paths.
Unsupported replay and missing/mismatched current authority reject before output or verification reliance; failed preparation preserves prior evidence.
Old production reports cannot supply missing current authority.

cases.title: Operational entrypoints enforce their selected identity and required gates
cases.risk: The hosted tag selects another name or commit from the checked source.

conditions: Use the tag fixture with its independently captured trusted commit and inspect actual release entrypoint composition.

when: Exercise matching/mismatching hosted ref, tag commit and checked HEAD; inspect command gate wiring.
then: Matching selected tag authority succeeds; mismatched names/commits reject.
The actual entrypoints expose and invoke their required identity and qualification checks. A source inspection does not claim hosted execution or public success.
